# 2.1.2 Elementwise Vector Operations

As the name suggests, elementwise operations are the operations that are performed across two elements of two different vectors(or a vector and scalar) according to the positions of the elements of those vector(s) or scalar. Note that to perform elementwise operations, both the vectors must be of the same length(except vector scaling where the scalar is a single variable).

Let us dive into some basic elementwise operations that can be performed on vectors. These include addition, subtraction, multiplication and scaling. 
\
\

## 2.1.2.1 Vector Addition

**Definition 2.1.2.1** (Vector Addition). \ Vector Addition is the element-wise sum of two vectors $\mathbf{u}, \mathbf{v} \in \mathbb{R}^n$ to yield another vector $\mathbf{w} \in \mathbb{R}^n$.
$$
\mathbf{u} + \mathbf{v} = \begin{bmatrix} u_1\\ u_2\\ \vdots\\ u_n \end{bmatrix} + \begin{bmatrix} v_1\\ v_2\\ \vdots\\ v_n \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} u_1 + v_1\\ u_2 + v_2\\ \vdots\\ u_n + v_n \end{bmatrix} \in \mathbb{R}^n
$$
\
Recall that $\mathbb{R}^n$ represents the $n$-dimensional set of real numbers and all vectors are represented in lowercase bold letters.

\
\

**Example 2.1.2.1**
$$
\begin{bmatrix} 5\\ 3\\ \end{bmatrix} + \begin{bmatrix} 2\\ 6\\ \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} 5 + 2\\ 3 + 6\\ \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} 7\\ 9\\ \end{bmatrix} \in \mathbb{R}^2
$$

\
\
\

## 2.1.2.2 Vector Scaling

**Definition 2.1.2.2** (Vector Scaling). \ Vector scaling is multipying each element $v_i$ of the vector $\mathbf{v} \in \mathbb{R}^n$ with a scalar  $\alpha \in \mathbb{R}$ to yeild another vector $\mathbf{w}$.
$$
\alpha \mathbf{v} = \alpha \begin{bmatrix} v_1\\ v_2\\ \vdots\\ v_n \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} \alpha v_1\\ \alpha v_2\\ \vdots\\ \alpha v_n \end{bmatrix} \in \mathbb{R}^n
$$

\
\

**Example 2.1.2.2**
$$
5 \begin{bmatrix} 4\\ 6\\ \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} 5*4\\ 5*6\\ \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} 20\\ 30\\ \end{bmatrix} \in \mathbb{R}^2
$$


## 2.1.2.3 Vector Subtraction

**Definition 2.1.2.3** (Vector Subtraction). \ Vector subtraction is the elementwise addition of a vector $\mathbf{u} \in \mathbb{R}^n$ with the vector $\mathbf{v} \in \mathbb{R}^n$ scaled by a factor of -1.
$$
\mathbf{u} - \mathbf{v} = \begin{bmatrix} u_1\\ u_2\\ \vdots\\ u_n \end{bmatrix} + -1 \begin{bmatrix} v_1\\ v_2\\ \vdots\\ v_n \end{bmatrix} = 
\begin{bmatrix} u_1\\ u_2\\ \vdots\\ u_n \end{bmatrix} + \begin{bmatrix} -v_1\\ -v_2\\ \vdots\\ -v_n \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} u_1 + (-v_1)\\ u_2 + (-v_2)\\ \vdots\\ u_n + (-v_n) \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} u_1 - v_1\\ u_2 - v_2\\ \vdots\\ u_n - v_n \end{bmatrix} \in \mathbb{R}^n
$$
\

**Example 2.1.2.3**
$$
\begin{bmatrix} 7\\ 3\\ \end{bmatrix} - \begin{bmatrix} 1\\ 8\\ \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} 7\\ 3 \end{bmatrix} + -1 \begin{bmatrix} 1\\ 8\\ \end{bmatrix} = 
\begin{bmatrix} 7\\ 3 \end{bmatrix} + \begin{bmatrix} -1\\ -8 \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} 7 + (-1)\\ 3 + (-8) \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} 7 - 1\\ 3 - 8 \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} 6\\ -5 \end{bmatrix} \in \mathbb{R}^2
$$

\
\

## 2.1.2.4 Scaled Vector Addition

**Definition 2.1.2.4** (Scaled Vector Addition). \ Scaled Vector Addition is the elementwise addition of a vector $\mathbf{u} \in \mathbb{R}^n$ with the vector $\mathbf{v} \in \mathbb{R}^n$ scaled by a factor of $\alpha$.
$$
\mathbf{u} + \alpha \mathbf{v} = \begin{bmatrix} u_1\\ u_2\\ \vdots\\ u_n \end{bmatrix} + \alpha \begin{bmatrix} v_1\\ v_2\\ \vdots\\ v_n \end{bmatrix} = 
\begin{bmatrix} u_1\\ u_2\\ \vdots\\ u_n \end{bmatrix} + \begin{bmatrix} \alpha v_1\\  \alpha v_2\\ \vdots\\ \alpha v_n \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} u_1 + \alpha v_1\\ u_2 + \alpha v_2\\ \vdots\\ u_n + \alpha v_n \end{bmatrix} \in \mathbb{R}^n
$$

It is same as vector subtraction when $\alpha$ = -1.
\
\
**Example 2.1.2.4**
$$
\begin{bmatrix} 6\\ 8\\ \end{bmatrix} + 4 \begin{bmatrix} 3\\ 5\\ \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} 6\\ 8 \end{bmatrix} + \begin{bmatrix} 4*3\\ 4*5 \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} 6 + 12\\ 8 + 20 \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} 18\\ 28 \end{bmatrix} \in \mathbb{R}^2
$$
\
\

## 2.1.2.5 Hadamard Product

**Definition 2.1.2.5** (Hadamard Product). \ The Hadamard product, also known as the elementwise product, is the component-wise multiplication of two vectors $\mathbf{u}, \mathbf{v} \in \mathbb{R}^n$ to yield another vector $\mathbf{w} \in \mathbb{R}^n$:
$$
\mathbf{u} \circ \mathbf{v} = \begin{bmatrix} u_1\\ u_2\\ \vdots\\ u_n \end{bmatrix} \circ \begin{bmatrix} v_1\\ v_2\\ \vdots\\ v_n \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} u_1 v_1\\ u_2 v_2\\ \vdots\\ u_n v_n \end{bmatrix} \in \mathbb{R}^n
$$

Note that the Hadamard product is different from the dot product, which results in a scalar, while hadamard product results in a vector.

\
\

**Example 2.1.2.5**
$$
\begin{bmatrix} 2\\ 4 \end{bmatrix} \circ \begin{bmatrix} 5\\ 3 \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} 2 \cdot 5\\ 4 \cdot 3 \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} 10\\ 12 \end{bmatrix} \in \mathbb{R}^2
$$
